texts.preamble: State vs . Bharat Bhushan on 15 October, 2022 In The Court Of Sh. Jitender: Metropoitan Magistrate01 : North : Rohini Courts : Delhi. State Vs. Bharat Bhushan Fir Number : 749/2014 Under Section : 279/338/304A Ipc. Police Station : Narela. Judgment
texts.facts: The case of the prosecution is that on 10/06/2014 at around 10:04 PM in front of FCA Godown near Railway Fatak, Narela, Delhi, (hereinafter "spot" or "the place of accident" or "the spot") one motorcycle bearing No. DLSE5033 (hereinafter the "offending vehicle") being driven in rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and personal safety of other and hit against a pedestrian namely Uday Shankar Pandey, due to the collusion, caused injuries resulting in his death and also caused grievous injuries to pillion rider of motorcycle namely Kulbhushan @ Ashu. The present FIR No.749/2014 was registered under section 279/338/304A Indian Penal Code (hereinafter "IPC") on the complaint of the HC Baljeet Singh. 2. On the basis of the investigation carried out by the police, chargesheet was filed under section 173 Cr.P.C in the court on 08/04/2016 and chargesheet and other relevant document were supplied to the accused in compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C to the satisfaction of the accused. 3. Notice for committing the offence punishable under section 279/338/304A IPC was served upon the accused on 11/01/2017 to which accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial. Thereafter, the matter was fixed for PE. PROSECUTION EVIDENCE 4. To prove it's case, prosecution has examined as many as 7 witnesses. PW 1 Shri Krishan and PW 3 Kulbhushan have been projected as eyewitness of the incident. The crux of their respective testimonies as follow: 4.1 PW1 Shri Krishan stated that, he used to sell CD, cassettes etc. in front of Anaj mandi, Narela. He does not remember the exact date, month and year of the incident but it was about 4 year ago. After closing his shop on the day of incident, he was going to his house in his car. When he reached near FCI godown, he stopped his car to drink the water. When he was drinking the water, he heard some noise of hitting something. He got down from the car and went behind and saw that public persons had gathered there on the spot and 2 persons were lying on the road. He made call at 100 No. There was a hotel nearby. Some person from the said hotel came in their car and took the injured persons to the hospital. This witness was cross examined by Ld.APP for the State after duly allowed by the court and he stated that IO took him to the spot and he was asked about the place of incident. He does not remember whether his statement was recorded or not. The incident took place on 10/06/2014 at about 10 PM. This witness denied a suggestion that he told to the IO when he reached a little ahead of FCI godown in front of Daily Needs Restaurant, one motorcycle bearing registration No. DL 11 SE 5033 yellow colour make pulser came in very rash and negligent manner and hit against one pedestrian who was crossing the road. He further denied the suggestion that he told to the IO due to the impact of the hitting, the motorcycle driver and pillion rider and the person who was hit fell down on the road and they suffered injuries. He further denied a suggestion that he told to the IO that he is the witness of incident. He was called by the IO and the site plan was prepared at his instance. This witness denied a suggestion that he identified the accused and at his identification the State vs . Bharat Bhushan on 15 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58167859/ 2 accused was arrested and his personal search was conducted. Accused and the photograph of the offending vehicle were shown to the witness and he stated that he is not able to identify the same as he did not see the incident. This witness was not crossexamined by the accused. 4.2 PW3 Kulbhushan stated that the incident took place on 10/06/2014. On that day, he along with his brother Bharat Bhushan (Accused) were going to buy 'Prasad' on their motorcycle bearing registration No. DL.......5033. When they reached at Bawana road near FCI godown, one person was crossing the road and from the opposite side one DTC bus was coming at high speed. On seeing the bus, the pedestrian starting running and was hit by the side of the bus. Due to that, the pedestrian fell down in front of their motorcycle. His brother Bharat Bhushan was driving the motorcycle and he was pillion rider. His brother applied sudden brakes and the motorcycle got disbalanced and he and his brother fell down on the road. He sustained injuries and the pedestrian was severely injured. There are dhaba near the spot. Accused shifted him and that pedestrian to SRHC hospital in the car of dhaba owner along with him. He was referred to LNJP hospital. He does not know anything else. This witness was cross examined by Ld. APP for the state at length and he stated that his brother was driving at normal speed of 3035 km/h. The accident was not happened due to the rash or negligent driving of his brother. He did not ask his brother to drive properly. His brother was driving the vehicle in proper manner. This witness denied the suggestion that his brother was driving the motorcycle at a high speed and in a zigzag manner and for that reason, the accident was caused. He further denied a suggestion that he warned his brother to drive the motorcycle in a proper manner as he was no driving properly. The injured was not hit by their motorcycle. The injured was fell down due to hit by DTC bus. Police did not record his statement. This witness again denied the suggestion that he is deliberately not disclosing the true facts as accused is his brother. He again denied a suggestion that during investigation he got recorded his statement. This witness was cross examined by Sh. Amit Punia on behalf of accused and the witness stated that when the deceased was hit by DTC bus, his brother applied sudden brakes their motorcycle got skid and because of that, he sustained injuries. 4.3 PW6 ASI Baljeet Singh stated that on 10/06/2014 he received a PCR call regarding the DD No. 103B and after receiving the information, he along with constable Sanjeev went to the spot, where they came to know that injured persons already shifted to SRHC hospital. They went to the hospital and he collected the MLC of both the injured persons. They came back to the spot but there was no public witness present. On the basis of DD entry, he prepared the Tehrir and send it to PS through constable Sanjeev for the registration of FIR. After registration of FIR, constable Sanjeev came back to the spot along with original Rukka and copy of FIR. He seized offending vehicle. This witness was cross examined by Sh. Sanjeev Deshwal on behalf of the accused and he stated that he has no clue about the negligence as he is not an eyewitness. There was no eyewitness and also, the offending vehicle was not found at the spot. Public person informed him that injured person was shifted to the SRHC hospital. He came back at the spot from the hospital and at that time, no State vs . Bharat Bhushan on 15 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58167859/ 3 eyewitness was present at the spot. He had made local enquiry at the spot then he found the offending vehicle. The offending vehicle took to the PS through a private tempo but the same fact has not mentioned in Tehrir and in his statement. Neither the driver of said tempo listed as eyewitness in prosecution list. Apart from these 3 witnesses, 4 other former and police witnesses were also examined and they were supported the case of the prosecution. Prosecution evidence was closed on 19/05/2022 and matter was listed for statement of accused U/S 313 Cr.P.C and same was recorded on 26/09/2022. STATEMENT OF ACCUSED 4. After recording the prosecution evidence all the incriminating facts and evidence were put before the accused and he pleaded that at the time of accident he was driving the offending vehicle in a normal speed and follow the traffic rules. The accident was caused by the driver of the DTC bus and not by him. The IO of the present case not conducted the investigation in fair and proper manner and IO booked him falsely in this case and further pleaded that he is innocent. Lastly, he said that he does not want lead any evidence.
texts.arguments: Let us peruse the provision of Section 279 IPC, which is as under : Section 279 Rash driving or riding on a public wayWhoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. State vs . Bharat Bhushan on 15 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58167859/ 4 Essentials Ingredients of Section 279 IPC (1). Driving or riding in a public way (2). Such driving or riding must be rash or negligent to the point of endangering human life or causing harm or injury to others. The Hon'ble Supreme court in the case titled Ravi Kapur v. State of Rajasthan, (2012) 9 SCC 284 observed that: "A rash act is primarily an overhasty act. It is opposed to a deliberate act. Still a rash act can be a deliberate act in the sense that it was done without due care and caution. Culpable rashness lies in running the risk of doing an act with recklessness and with indifference as to the consequences. Criminal negligence is the failure to exercise duty with reasonable and proper care and precaution guarding against injury to the public generally or to any individual in particular. It is the imperative duty of the driver of a vehicle to adopt such reasonable and proper care and precaution." The Hon'ble Supreme court further observed that Ravi Kapur (supra); "The court has to adopt another parameter i.e. "reasonable care" in determining the question of negligence or contributory negligence. The doctrine of reasonable care imposes an obligation or a duty upon a person (for example a driver) to care for the pedestrian on the road and this duty attains a higher degree when the pedestrians happen to be children of tender years. It is axiomatic to say that while driving a vehicle on a public way, there is an implicit duty cast on the drivers to see that their driving does not endanger the life of the right users of the road, may be either vehicular users or pedestrians. They are expected to take sufficient care to avoid danger to others." 7. "Whether accused Bharat Bhushan has committed the offence causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety under section 338 IPC?" Let us peruse the provision of Section 338 IPC, which is as under : Section 338: Causing grievous hurt by act endangering life or personal safety of others: Whoever causes grievous hurt to any person by doing any act so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life, or the personal safety of others, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both. Essentials Ingredients of Section 338 IPC (1). Accused did an act rashly or negligently. (2). Act endangered human life or the personal safety of others. (3). Such act cause grievous hurt. State vs . Bharat Bhushan on 15 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58167859/ 5 8. "Whether accused Bharat Bhushan has caused death by such act with rash or negligence act under section 304A ?" Let us peruse the provision 304A IPC, which is as under : Section304A. Causing death by negligence.-- Whoever causes the death of any person by doing any rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine, or with both." Essentials ingredients of the section 304A (1). There must be death of person in question (2). The death must be caused by the accused (3). The death must be caused due to rash or negligent act of accused; and (4). Act of the accused must not amount to culpable homicide. In Alister Anthony Pareira v. State of Maharashtra's [(2012) 2 SCC 648] Section 304A applies to cases where there is no intention to cause death and no knowledge that the act done in all probability will cause death. The provision applies only to such acts which are rash and negligent and are directly cause of death of another person. Negligence and rashness are essential elements under Section 304A. Rashness means doing an act with the consciousness of a risk that evil consequences will follow but with the hope that it will not Negligence is a breach of duty imposed by law. Criminal negligence on the other hand, is the gross and culpable neglect or failure to exercise that reasonable and proper care and precaution to guard against injury either to the public generally or to an individual in particular, which, having regard to all the circumstances out of which the charge has arisen it was the imperative duty of the accused person to have adopted." 9. In, Dalbir Singh v. State of Haryana[(2000) 5 SCC 82 : State vs . Bharat Bhushan on 15 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58167859/ 6 2000 SCC (Cri) 1208], the Apex Court was concerned with a case where the accused was held guilty of the offence under Section 304A IPC. The Court made the following observations: When automobiles have become death traps any leniency shown to drivers who are found guilty of rash driving would be at the risk of steering of automobiles, particularly professional drivers, must be kept under constant reminders of their duty to adopt utmost care and also of the consequences befalling them in cases of dereliction. One of the most effective ways of keeping such drivers under mental vigil is to maintain a deterrent element in the sentencing sphere. Any latitude shown to them in that sphere would tempt them to make driving frivolous and a frolic." FINDINGS 10. In the case titled as Dr. S. L. Goswami vs State of Madhya Pradesh, 1972 Supreme Court Cases (Cri) 258, Hon'ble Apex Court has held that: (i) The onus of proving all the ingredients of an offence is always upon the prosecution and at no stage does is shift to the accused. It is no part of the prosecution duty to somehow hook the crook. Where the onus shifts to the accused, and the evidence on his behalf probabilizes the plea he will be entitled to the benefit of reasonable doubt". ( iii) That death of any person must have been caused; (iv) and it must have been caused by rash or negligent act/driving of the accused. In Mohan Singh v. State of Madhya Pradesh (1999) 2 SCC 428 the Supreme Court pointed out: The principles relating to appreciation of the evidence of interested and related witnesses, as explained in the above decisions, may be summarised as under: State vs . Bharat Bhushan on 15 October, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/58167859/ 8 (a) Once the Court is satisfied that the witness who is related to the victim is not a chance witness, then the evidence of such witness would have to be examined from the point of view of probabilities. The version of such witness as to the assault has to be carefully scrutinised. (b) Though the witness may be hostile to the assailant, it is not likely that such witness would deliberately omit to name the real assailant and substitute in his place the name of enemy of the family out of malice. (c) It is not improbable that in giving evidence, such a witness may name the real assailant and may add other persons out of malice and enmity and that is a factor which has to be borne in mind in appreciating the evidence of interested witnesses. (d) Merely because a witness is shown to be a relative of the deceased, and it is also shown that the witness shared the hostility of the victim towards the assailant, it cannot be said that the evidence of such witness would never be accepted unless it is corroborated on material particulars. (e) Where the witnesses are interested, the court should approach their evidence with care and caution in order to exclude the possibility of false implication. In Jayabalan v. UT of Pondicherry (2010) 1 SCC 199, the Supreme Court held as under: "23. We are of the considered view that in cases where the court is called upon to deal with the evidence of the interested witnesses, the approach of the court, while appreciating the evidence of such witnesses must not be pedantic. The court must be cautious in appreciating and accepting the evidence given by the interested witnesses but the court must not be suspicious of such evidence. The primary endeavour of the court must be to look for consistency." Circumstantial evidence 15. Circumstantial evidence is indirect evidence that does not, on its face, prove a fact in issue but gives rise to a logical inference that the fact exists. Circumstantial evidence requires drawing additional reasonable inferences in order to support the claim. When no other conclusive evidence are present to establish the liability of the accused, the prosecution shall rely upon the circumstantial evidence corroborating with other evidence. 9 In Sharad Birdhi chand Sarda v. State of Maharashtra (1984) 4 SCC 116 153, the Apex court has observed about the circumstantial evidence that: "(i) The circumstances from which the conclusion of guilt is to be drawn should be fully established. The circumstances concerned 'must' or 'should' and not 'may be established': (ii) The facts so established should be consistent only with the hypothesis of the guilt of the accused, that is to say, they should not be explainable on any other hypothesis except that the accused is guilty: (iii)The circumstances should be of a conclusive nature and tendency: (iv)They should exclude every possible hypothesis except the one to be proved and; (v) There must be a chain of evidence so complete as not to leave any reasonable ground for the conclusion consistent with the innocence of the accused and must show that in all human probably the act must have been done by the accused". CONCLUSION 16.
